title: mcp read_file: when the worker ceiling cuts a read before page 1, the answer is content none with a note saying "after page 0 … so the text is partial"
body:
repo:objectstack#4 · os-lizheng · session_012MmDsS4GoHCgYwA2uv3n3C

Filing gate: class a, an out-of-scope finding of the #34758 dev round (PR #34853, report 6950149326), measured by that dev through `read_file` under synthetic load. ⛔ Not a claim. Grading and `domain:*` are triage's.

Suggested-grade: p3 · a misleading sentence on a rare path; no data is lost

## 维护者速读

- 现象:AI 通过 MCP 读一个 PDF 时，如果 worker 在读完第 1 页之前就被墙钟上限掐断，回答是「没有内容」，但附带的说明写着「在第 0 页后停在 CPU 预算上，所以文字是部分的」。实际一个字都没给，说明却说给了一部分。
- 为什么要修:agent 会照这句话去理解结果(以为拿到了部分文本),说法和实际不符。
- 需要你做的：无(分诊定级)。

## What (measured by the dev, not re-measured by the seat)

Under load, `read_file` through `MCPServerRuntime.callTool` answered `content: 'none'` with the note `Reading stopped at the CPU-time budget for one file (30 ms) after page 0 of 120, so the text is partial.` Landing point named by the dev: `packages/mcp/src/file-content.ts`, `stoppedExtractionAnswer` → `pdfAnswer([], numPages, note)` when the worker's wall-clock ceiling (5 budgets of real time) fires before the first page. The docx path is analogous. Without load, a PDF whose page 1 outruns 5 budgets of wall time reaches it.

## Done when

A ceiling stop before the first page answers with a sentence that does not claim partial text (and says the read stopped before any page), pinned for PDF and Word with a deterministic clock, as PR #34853 does for the budget case.

## Notes

Lands after PR #34853 (same test file).

Dedupe: `stoppedExtractionAnswer` (1 hit, #34758 itself); `"after page 0"` (58 hits, phrase too generic to match; none names this note).
